title: Unscripted Producer Rachel Tung Renews ABC & Hulu Development Deal (EXCLUSIVE)

whatHappening: Veteran unscripted producer Rachel Tung has renewed her development deal with ABC and Hulu, securing continued opportunities to create original programming for Disney's broadcast and streaming platforms. Under the refreshed agreement, Tung will develop new projects while serving as showrunner on select series.
whoInvolved: Rachel Tung is an established unscripted television producer with a track record of developing reality and documentary-style content. ABC and Hulu, both part of The Walt Disney Company, are the broadcast and streaming partners backing her production efforts.
whyMatters: The renewal signals Disney's confidence in Tung's ability to generate compelling unscripted content across multiple platforms at a time when networks are heavily investing in reality programming. Long-term, this deal positions Tung to shape the unscripted landscape on both traditional broadcast and streaming services, where demand for diverse, original programming continues to grow.
articleBody:
Veteran unscripted producer Rachel Tung has secured a renewed development deal with ABC and Hulu, according to Variety, reflecting ongoing confidence in her ability to create original programming for Disney's portfolio. The extended agreement allows Tung to continue developing unscripted projects while taking on showrunner responsibilities for select series across the network and streaming service.

Tung's career in unscripted television has established her as a capable producer capable of navigating both the demands of broadcast television and the distinct requirements of streaming platforms. The renewal comes at a moment when traditional networks and streamers are competing intensely for original content that can differentiate their offerings and retain audiences.

Under the terms of the renewed deal, Tung will focus on developing original unscripted programming tailored to ABC and Hulu's distinct audiences and programming strategies. Her role as showrunner on select projects indicates that the partnership values not only her creative development capabilities but also her ability to oversee production and maintain creative vision through execution.

The agreement underscores Disney's commitment to maintaining relationships with established producers who have demonstrated success in the unscripted space. As streaming services and traditional networks continue to blur in their content strategies, producers like Tung who can work effectively across both formats are increasingly valuable to major media companies.

Tung's renewed deal comes amid broader industry trends of networks retaining proven creative talent through multi-year agreements. Such arrangements provide stability for producers while allowing studios to maintain pipelines of original content development.

title: ‘Harry Potter’ Series Star Bel Powley Says ‘I Strongly Disagree With J.K. Rowling’s Views on Gender’: ‘The Trans Community Deserve Safety and Dignity’
summary: “Harry Potter” series star Bel Powley has spoken out about author J.K. Rowling’s controversial views on gender, saying she “strongly disagrees” with them. Powley is playing Petunia Dursley in HBO’s highly anticipated TV adaptation of the beloved books, the first season of which…
whatHappening: Bel Powley, cast as Petunia Dursley in HBO's upcoming Harry Potter TV adaptation, has publicly stated she strongly disagrees with author J.K. Rowling's views on gender and is affirming support for the transgender community.
whoInvolved: Bel Powley is an actress set to play Petunia Dursley in HBO's adaptation of the Harry Potter series, the best-selling book franchise in history with over 600 million copies sold worldwide. J.K. Rowling is the British author behind the seven-volume Harry Potter series and has faced sustained controversy over her public statements regarding gender and sex.
whyMatters: The statement highlights ongoing tensions between the creative legacy of the Harry Potter franchise and its author's publicly stated positions on gender identity, an issue that has divided cast members and fans since Rowling's statements began circulating years ago. As major productions like HBO's new adaptation move forward, cast members' willingness to openly distance themselves from the author signals the enduring nature of this cultural divide within the franchise's fanbase and industry.
articleBody:
Actress Bel Powley has become the latest member of the Harry Potter universe to publicly distance herself from author J.K. Rowling's stance on gender issues. Powley, who will portray Petunia Dursley in HBO's highly anticipated television adaptation of the beloved book series, stated that she "strongly disagrees" with Rowling's views and emphasized that "the trans community deserve safety and dignity," according to Variety.

Rowling's positions on gender and sex have sparked significant controversy in recent years, drawing criticism from LGBTQ+ advocates and some cast and crew members associated with the franchise. The author, whose Harry Potter series became the best-selling book series in history with over 600 million copies sold globally, has maintained her stance on these issues despite the backlash. Her comments have created a notable divide between the cultural phenomenon she created and portions of its fanbase.

HBO's new Harry Potter television adaptation represents a major expansion of the franchise, which has already generated enormous revenue through the eight-film series produced by Warner Bros. Pictures from 2001 to 2011, along with the Fantastic Beasts prequel films beginning in 2016. As production moves forward on this new iteration, statements like Powley's reflect the ongoing challenge facing major productions tied to Rowling's work: navigating the author's influence on the material while addressing her public positions that some cast members find objectionable.

Powley's comments add to a pattern of Harry Potter actors and creators openly disagreeing with or condemning Rowling's statements. The franchise's cultural significance—spanning multiple generations of readers and viewers—has made these tensions particularly visible and consequential for the industry and fanbase alike. HBO's casting of Powley and her subsequent statement suggest the network is proceeding with the adaptation even amid these ongoing controversies.

The tension between Rowling's literary creation and her public persona presents a unique challenge for the entertainment industry. As beloved franchises navigate complex social and political landscapes, the question of how casts and creators engage with controversial figures behind the material continues to evolve, with performers increasingly using their platforms to articulate their own values.

title: ‘Brave New Love’ Review: Infidelity Isn’t the End in an Unusual, Open-Minded Marital Drama
summary: “I would never fall in love if I was in a good relationship.” So says one participant in the women’s church group where Copenhagen-based wife and mother Kate (Kathrine Thorborg Johansen) confesses that she’s been having a three-year affair with another man, and doesn’t much…
whatHappening: A new marital drama film explores unconventional relationship dynamics when a wife confesses a three-year affair to her church group, challenging traditional notions of fidelity and commitment. The film examines whether infidelity must spell the end of a marriage, presenting a more nuanced and open-minded perspective on modern relationships.
whoInvolved: The film stars Kathrine Thorborg Johansen as Kate, a Copenhagen-based wife and mother who becomes the focal point of the narrative. The production comes from Variety, a major entertainment industry publication covering film reviews and criticism.
whyMatters: The film's willingness to explore infidelity without moral absolutism reflects evolving conversations about marriage, commitment, and personal fulfillment in contemporary society. By presenting a protagonist who doesn't abandon her relationship despite a long-term affair, the story challenges audiences to reconsider what healthy relationships might look like beyond traditional frameworks.
articleBody:
A new marital drama challenges conventional wisdom about infidelity and relationship dissolution by presenting a more nuanced exploration of modern marriage. In the film, Kate, a wife and mother living in Copenhagen, makes a striking confession to her women's church group: she has been conducting a three-year affair with another man. Rather than treating this revelation as a narrative endpoint, the film uses it as a starting point to examine deeper questions about love, commitment, and what it means to sustain a relationship through unconventional circumstances.

The premise hinges on a provocative statement from one of the film's participants: "I would never fall in love if I was in a good relationship." This observation sets the tone for what becomes a complex meditation on desire, dissatisfaction, and the possibility of moving beyond infidelity rather than being destroyed by it. According to Variety, the film approaches its subject matter with unusual open-mindedness, refusing easy moral judgments about Kate's choices and instead focusing on the emotional and relational terrain that led her to seek connection elsewhere.

The setting of a women's church group adds another layer to the narrative, creating a space where personal confessions intersect with spiritual and moral frameworks. The group becomes a sounding board for examining questions about forgiveness, judgment, and what genuine support might look like when confronted with messy human reality. Kate's willingness to confess suggests a desire to move beyond secrecy, even if it means exposing herself to judgment from those close to her.

By centering on a protagonist who maintains her marriage despite an affair rather than fleeing it, the film implicitly questions whether the end of infidelity must always mean the end of the relationship. This perspective acknowledges that people are capable of loving multiple people, or of seeking fulfillment in ways that complicate traditional marriage vows, without necessarily viewing the marriage itself as fundamentally broken or unsalvageable.

The film's willingness to sit with discomfort rather than resolve it quickly reflects a broader shift in contemporary storytelling about relationships. Rather than delivering moral clarity, it invites viewers to consider the gap between how we believe relationships should function and how they actually do, in all their messy, contradictory humanity.

whatHappening: Sadhguru, an Indian yogi and spiritual leader, is collaborating with Graphic India to produce an animated feature film called "Shiva: The Adiyogi." The film will retell the origin story of the Hindu god Shiva, portraying him as the first yogi, with Sadhguru and Graphic India founder Sharad Devarajan sharing story credit.
whoInvolved: Sadhguru (Jagadish Vasudev) is an Indian guru and founder of the Isha Foundation, established in 1992, which operates an ashram and yoga center in Coimbatore offering educational and spiritual programs. Graphic India is an animation studio known for creating India-focused animated content.
whyMatters: This collaboration represents a significant intersection of spiritual education and mainstream media, bringing Hindu philosophical concepts to a global animated audience. The project leverages Sadhguru's established platform—he is a New York Times bestselling author and international speaker—to reach viewers beyond traditional spiritual forums.
articleBody:
Indian yogi and mystic Sadhguru is joining forces with animation studio Graphic India to develop "Shiva: The Adiyogi," an animated feature that will explore the origin story of Shiva, the Hindu deity, presenting him as the first yogi. According to Variety, Sadhguru and Graphic India founder Sharad Devarajan are sharing story credit on the project, positioning it as a collaboration between a spiritual authority and a creative studio.

Sadhguru, whose formal name is Jagadish Vasudev, has established himself as a prominent figure in global wellness and spirituality. He founded the Isha Foundation in 1992, which operates an ashram and yoga center based in Coimbatore, India, dedicated to educational and spiritual pursuits. Beyond his work at the foundation, Sadhguru has been teaching yoga since 1982 and has authored two New York Times bestsellers: "Inner Engineering: A Yogi's Guide to Joy" and "Karma: A Yogi's Guide to Crafting Your Destiny." His visibility extends to international speaking engagements, where he regularly addresses global audiences on spiritual and wellness topics.

Graphic India, the studio spearheading the animation production, has built a reputation for creating animated content centered on Indian narratives and mythology. By pairing with Sadhguru, the studio is tapping into both his spiritual credibility and his substantial global following to shape the film's creative direction and authenticity.

The project reflects a growing trend of blending spiritual traditions with contemporary entertainment formats. By animating the philosophical narrative of Shiva as the original yogi, the film aims to make ancient Hindu spiritual concepts accessible to modern audiences, particularly younger viewers who may engage more readily with animated storytelling than traditional religious or philosophical texts.

The partnership also underscores Sadhguru's expanding influence beyond spiritual teaching into media and entertainment, leveraging his platform to reach new demographics and present Hindu philosophy through a popular culture medium.

title: Ariana Grande Debuts at No. 1 on Album Chart With ‘Petal,’ Earning Her Best First-Week Numbers in Seven Years

whatHappening: Ariana Grande has secured her seventh No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 chart with her new project "Petal," which debuted atop the rankings with 295,000 equivalent album units. This marks her strongest first-week performance in seven years.
whoInvolved: Ariana Grande is an American singer and songwriter known for her four-octave vocal range and influential role in popular music. The Billboard 200 is the primary weekly chart ranking the 200 most popular music albums and EPs in the United States, published by Billboard magazine to measure commercial success and cultural resonance.
whyMatters: Grande's chart dominance underscores her sustained commercial power and relevance in the music industry after a seven-year gap in achieving her best opening-week numbers. The album's strong debut and surrounding cultural conversation demonstrate continued audience investment in her work, signaling robust demand for her music despite the competitive modern streaming landscape.
articleBody:
Ariana Grande has achieved a significant milestone with the debut of her new album "Petal" at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 chart. The project opened with 295,000 equivalent album units, representing her strongest first-week performance since 2017, according to Variety. This marks Grande's seventh No. 1 album on the prestigious chart, further solidifying her status as one of the most successful recording artists of her generation.

The Billboard 200 has been the industry standard for measuring album success in the United States since acquiring its current name in 1992. The chart ranks the 200 most popular music albums and EPs weekly, providing a definitive snapshot of commercial performance and audience preference. Grande's repeated success on this chart reflects both her artistic credibility and her ability to mobilize her fanbase around new releases.

"Petal" and its accompanying songs and music videos have generated substantial conversation across media and social platforms, contributing to the album's commercial momentum. This cultural engagement suggests that the project has resonated beyond typical chart metrics, capturing audience attention through both musical content and visual presentation. Grande's known four-octave vocal range and her position as an influential figure in popular music continue to define her artistic identity.

The opening-week figure represents Grande's best performance this decade, a significant achievement given the evolving landscape of music consumption and the increased competition from other high-profile releases. Her ability to accumulate 295,000 equivalent album units in a single week demonstrates the enduring commercial strength of her fanbase and her standing in the industry. Publications such as Rolling Stone and Billboard have previously recognized Grande among the greatest artists in history, and this chart performance reaffirms that critical assessment with tangible commercial data.

title: Protest at the Locarno Film Festival Remembers 60,000 Names of the Dead of Gaza
summary: Locarno became the latest film festival to see protests at the continuing situation in Gaza and Palestine’s Occupied Territories. While music from the Campari Lounge boomed into the evening, approximately 100 demonstrators unwound a shroud bearing the names of 60,000 people who…
whatHappening: Approximately 100 protesters at the Locarno Film Festival in Switzerland unfurled a shroud bearing 60,000 names representing Palestinians killed in Gaza, marking the latest film festival to host demonstrations over the ongoing conflict.
whoInvolved: The Locarno International Film Festival, founded in 1946 and held annually in Locarno, Switzerland, is one of the world's major film festivals featuring competitive and non-competitive sections across multiple formats. The protesters are demonstrating against the Gaza–Israel conflict, which has claimed over 73,000 Palestinian lives according to recent figures.
whyMatters: The protest underscores how the Gaza conflict has become a focal point for activism even within cultural institutions traditionally focused on cinema and art. As film festivals increasingly become venues for political expression, the incident reflects broader tension between cultural programming and calls for solidarity with Palestinians.
articleBody:
The Locarno International Film Festival became the latest major cultural event to host demonstrations over the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and the Occupied Territories. According to Variety, approximately 100 demonstrators gathered at the Swiss festival to unfurl a shroud inscribed with the names of 60,000 Palestinians killed in the conflict, staging their protest even as music from the festival's Campari Lounge continued in the background.

The Locarno festival, which has been held annually since its founding in 1946, is among the world's most prestigious film festivals, screening works across feature narratives, documentaries, shorts, avant-garde pieces, and retrospective programs. The festival's iconic Piazza Grande outdoor venue seats 8,000 spectators and serves as a cultural gathering point in the Alpine town. The decision by activists to stage their demonstration at such a prominent venue reflects the growing visibility of Gaza-related protests across multiple sectors of society.

The Gaza–Israel conflict has resulted in staggering loss of life. Since 1948, when approximately 200,000 Palestinian refugees first settled in Gaza following displacement, the region has been marked by repeated military conflicts. The current war has claimed the lives of over 73,000 Palestinians, a figure that exceeds the combined death toll of all other wars within the broader Israeli–Palestinian conflict.

The choice to display 60,000 names on a shroud transforms an abstract casualty figure into a tangible representation of individual losses. By staging this memorial at a film festival—a space dedicated to storytelling and human experience—the protesters sought to connect the artistic mission of cinema with the human cost of the ongoing conflict. The contrast between the festival's celebratory atmosphere and the solemn nature of the protest highlights the tension between cultural programming and political reality.

title: ‘Donkey Princess’ Review: A Princess Escapes the Kingdom, but Not the Patriarchy, in an Inventive, Shape-Shifting Fairytale
summary: Chilean duo Cristobal León and Joaquín Cociña made a dream nightmare debut with “The Wolf House,” a stop-motion fantasy that turned heads both with its wholly original design — incorporating claymation, puppetry and papier-mâché to palpably handmade but immersively surreal…
whatHappening: Chilean filmmaker duo Cristobal León and Joaquín Cociña have created "Donkey Princess," a new stop-motion fairytale that subverts traditional princess narratives. The film follows a princess who escapes her kingdom but discovers that freedom from her realm does not liberate her from patriarchal constraints.
whoInvolved: Cristobal León and Joaquín Cociña are a Chilean stop-motion animator and filmmaker duo based in Santiago who have collaborated since 2007. They gained international recognition with their 2018 debut feature film "The Wolf House," which combined claymation, puppetry, and papier-mâché techniques to create a visually distinctive and surreal work.
whyMatters: The film represents another ambitious venture from a filmmaking duo known for pushing the boundaries of stop-motion animation and fairy tale storytelling. By centering on how escape from physical confinement doesn't necessarily dismantle deeper systemic constraints, the work engages with contemporary discussions about gender and power in a distinctly artistic context.
articleBody:
Cristobal León and Joaquín Cociña, the Chilean filmmaking duo behind the acclaimed stop-motion feature "The Wolf House," have returned with "Donkey Princess," a new fairytale that interrogates the limits of female liberation within patriarchal systems. The film follows a princess who manages to escape the confines of her kingdom, only to discover that physical escape does not automatically free her from the patriarchal structures that define her world.

Leon and Cociña, who have been collaborating since 2007 and are based in Santiago de Chile, first gained international attention with their 2018 debut "The Wolf House." That film showcased their distinctive visual approach, layering claymation, puppetry, and papier-mâché to create a wholly original aesthetic that felt simultaneously handmade and immersively surreal. According to Variety, the duo's new work continues this inventive approach with shape-shifting elements that deepen the fairytale's thematic complexity.

The two filmmakers have built their practice around rethinking children's literature and fairytale narratives, often repositioning their visual aesthetics and storytelling conventions for contemporary audiences. Their work extends beyond animation into drawings, installations, and written texts, reflecting a multimedia approach to their artistic practice. This multidisciplinary background informs how they approach "Donkey Princess," using the fantasy genre as a vehicle for examining questions of agency and constraint.

"Donkey Princess" presents its central character's escape not as a triumphant conclusion but as the beginning of a more complex reckoning with systemic power. The film's shape-shifting visual language—a signature element of León and Cociña's methodology—mirrors this thematic focus on transformation without genuine change. Rather than offering a simple narrative of female rebellion, the work suggests that escaping a physical location requires a fundamentally different kind of escape from the ideological systems that govern one's existence.

The film's engagement with fairytale tropes reflects León and Cociña's broader artistic commitment to excavating and recontextualizing narratives that have traditionally reinforced particular social structures. By placing a princess at the center of a story that complicates rather than celebrates her liberation, they create space for audiences to examine the often-invisible architecture of patriarchal power.

title: Naseeruddin Shah, Gurvinder Singh Turn a Village’s Real Grief Into Locarno Competition Title ‘Rehmat’: ‘It’s Important That These Films Get Made’
summary: The family living in the house that “Rehmat” uses as Rashid Ali’s ancestral home lost a son to a drug overdose shortly after Indian filmmaker Gurvinder Singh and his crew first met them. Singh tells Variety, “The actual family that lives there lost their 19-year-old son after we…
whatHappening: Filmmaker Gurvinder Singh and veteran actor Naseeruddin Shah have created "Rehmat," a film that transforms real tragedy into art—the family whose home serves as the film's setting lost their 19-year-old son to a drug overdose after Singh first met them. The film is now competing at the prestigious Locarno Film Festival.
whoInvolved: Naseeruddin Shah is a three-time National Film Award winner and recipient of the Padma Bhushan, known for his work in parallel cinema and international productions. Director Gurvinder Singh is an Indian filmmaker whose work has brought him to major international festivals.
whyMatters: The film represents cinema's power to honor real human suffering while telling important stories about addiction and loss in rural India. By centering the authentic grief of a real family, "Rehmat" raises questions about filmmaking ethics and the responsibility artists bear when depicting tragedy.
articleBody:
Filmmaker Gurvinder Singh and actor Naseeruddin Shah have created "Rehmat," a film now in competition at the Locarno International Film Festival that grapples with profound loss in an unexpected way. The production used an actual family's ancestral home as the setting for the character Rashid Ali's house—a decision that took on devastating significance when the family lost their 19-year-old son to a drug overdose shortly after Singh and his crew first made contact with them.

According to Variety, Singh has spoken openly about how this real tragedy became intertwined with the fictional narrative. Rather than abandon the project, the filmmakers proceeded with a deepened commitment to honoring the family's actual grief. The convergence of the family's real loss and the film's thematic content around death and mourning created an authenticity that Singh felt obligated to preserve.

Naseeruddin Shah, a recipient of three National Film Awards and the Volpi Cup for Best Actor at the Venice Film Festival, has built a career on selecting roles in parallel cinema that engage with complex human experiences. His involvement in "Rehmat" reflects his long commitment to films that examine India's social realities with unflinching honesty. The Government of India honored him with the Padma Bhushan in 2003 for his contributions to Indian cinema.

The Locarno International Film Festival, held annually in Switzerland since 1946, provides a significant platform for world cinema. By competing at Locarno, "Rehmat" joins a selective group of films that the festival's international programmers have deemed essential to screen. The festival's inclusion of the film signals recognition of its artistic and human importance.

Singh's statement that "it's important that these films get made" underscores his belief that cinema has a responsibility to tell stories that mainstream commercial filmmaking often avoids. Films dealing with addiction, rural hardship, and loss require the kind of creative courage and emotional maturity that parallel cinema has historically championed in India. The collaboration between Shah and Singh represents a commitment to that tradition.

title: Perez Hilton ‘Will Require Surgery’ After Live Stream Incident, Family Demands Media ‘Cease Photographing Perez’s Children’
summary: Perez Hilton’s family released a statement on Saturday updating fans about the blogger’s health after he appeared to commit self-harm during a TikTok livestream. “Perez’s condition remains serious but stable,” read the statement, which was released on Hilton’s website. “He…
whatHappening: Perez Hilton is in serious but stable condition following an apparent self-harm incident during a TikTok livestream. His family has issued a statement indicating he will require surgery, and they are urging media outlets to stop photographing his children.
whoInvolved: Perez Hilton (Mario Armando Lavandeira Jr.) is an American blogger and media personality known for his celebrity gossip blog, which covers tabloid photos and celebrity news. His family has released a public statement addressing his health and privacy concerns.
whyMatters: The incident highlights the personal toll of life in the public eye and raises concerns about mental health, online platform safety, and the boundaries between public figures and their families. The family's plea for media restraint reflects broader tensions over paparazzi practices and the protection of minors whose parents are public figures.
articleBody:
Perez Hilton's family released a statement on Saturday providing an update on the blogger's health following an apparent self-harm incident that occurred during a TikTok livestream. According to Variety, the statement confirmed that "Perez's condition remains serious but stable" and indicated that he will require surgery. The statement was released on Hilton's official website and addressed concerns from fans and the public about the incident.

Alongside the health update, Hilton's family made a direct appeal to media outlets and paparazzi, demanding that they "cease photographing Perez's children." The request underscores the family's desire to shield the children from the intense media scrutiny that typically accompanies coverage of celebrity incidents. This boundary-setting reflects growing awareness about the vulnerability of minors connected to public figures.

Hilton, whose real name is Mario Armando Lavandeira Jr., built his career as a blogger and media personality chronicling celebrity gossip and tabloid culture. His blog became known for posts covering celebrity news and for the practice of posting tabloid photos with his own captions or illustrated "doodles." Over the years, the blog has received controversy for its editorial approach and its role in amplifying celebrity coverage across media platforms.

The incident marks a significant moment for Hilton personally and raises broader questions about the mental health pressures faced by those who have built careers in the entertainment media landscape. The nature of constant public attention and the demands of maintaining relevance in digital spaces can create substantial psychological strain, particularly when a public figure's personal struggles become the subject of media coverage.

As Hilton awaits surgery and recovers, his family's statement signals their intent to prioritize his healing while maintaining a protective stance toward his children. The explicit request for media outlets to refrain from photographing his family members represents a clear demarcation between Hilton's public role as a media personality and the private lives of his dependents.

title: ‘Ketticè’ Review: An Amusing, Original Portrait of Adolescent Ennui Against a Backdrop of Adult Cluelessness
summary: Monica Bellucci’s sneer is a thing of wonder, so why have so few directors used it properly? When allowed full rein to her sense of irony, as given her by Giovanni Tortorici in “Ketticè,” Bellucci has few equals in her ability to project self-aware drama queen with just the…
whatHappening: Variety reviews "Ketticè," a new film directed by Giovanni Tortorici that explores adolescent dissatisfaction and generational disconnect. The film stars Monica Bellucci in a role that showcases her distinctive talent for ironic, self-aware dramatic performance.
whoInvolved: Monica Bellucci, an Italian actress with a long career spanning Italian, American, British, and French films, takes a lead role in "Ketticè." Director Giovanni Tortorici helms the project, crafting a portrait of teenage ennui set against parental incomprehension.
whyMatters: The film's fresh approach to adolescent storytelling—filtered through adult dysfunction—offers audiences a distinctive take on coming-of-age narratives. Bellucci's performance demonstrates the versatility of an accomplished actor whose particular gifts for irony and dramatic self-awareness have been underutilized by many directors.
articleBody:
Monica Bellucci's distinctive on-screen presence has long been a calling card of her acting repertoire, yet according to Variety, few directors have fully capitalized on her most potent weapon: her sneer. In "Ketticè," director Giovanni Tortorici appears to understand precisely what to do with this talent. The film presents an amusing and original examination of adolescent ennui, viewed through the lens of adult cluelessness, with Bellucci given full creative rein to deploy her considerable sense of irony.

Bellucci's career trajectory—from fashion model to international film presence—has taken her through diverse genres and languages across Italian, American, British, and French productions. Yet her ability to project a self-aware drama queen sensibility, paired with genuine emotional depth, remains one of cinema's underutilized resources. When a director grants her the space to fully explore this dimension of her craft, the results are difficult to match.

"Ketticè" represents precisely the kind of project that allows Bellucci's particular strengths to flourish. The film's premise—positioning adolescent disenchantment against a backdrop of parental bewilderment—creates fertile ground for her brand of ironic observation. Rather than playing the scenario straight, she inhabits it with the kind of knowing distance that transforms a potentially familiar narrative into something fresh and engaging.

The film's approach to generational tension suggests that neither teenagers nor adults possess a monopoly on confusion or self-delusion. By centering Bellucci's performance—one that embraces irony rather than fighting it—Tortorici has crafted a work that acknowledges the comedy inherent in the human condition, particularly the gap between how adolescents perceive themselves and how adults perceive them.

For viewers seeking coming-of-age stories that avoid sentimentality while remaining fundamentally human, "Ketticè" offers something distinct. The film's success hinges significantly on Bellucci's willingness to embrace her natural instincts for dramatic irony, suggesting that perhaps the real question isn't whether she possesses these gifts, but rather why the directing community has been so slow to request them.

title: ‘I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming’ Review: An Affecting Trans Relationship Drama Brings Fresh Perspective to the War in Ukraine
summary: Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine has prompted a wealth of urgent nonfiction filmmaking documenting the harsh realities of life under siege, but comparatively little dramatic storytelling — a space that the new German-Ukrainian production “I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming” occupies…
whatHappening: A new German-Ukrainian dramatic film titled "I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming" explores a trans relationship against the backdrop of Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The film represents a rare example of fictional storytelling addressing the war, filling a gap left by the surge of documentary filmmaking.
whoInvolved: The film is a German-Ukrainian co-production that tells the story of a trans couple navigating their relationship during wartime. While specific filmmakers and cast members are not detailed in available information, the production brings together creative talent from both nations to address the human dimensions of the conflict.
whyMatters: The film offers a fresh dramatic perspective on the Ukraine war at a moment when most artistic response has focused on documentary realism. By centering a trans relationship within the conflict's human toll, it expands the narrative landscape around one of Europe's largest conflicts since World War II and demonstrates how fiction can illuminate personal stories often overshadowed by military and political coverage.
articleBody:
Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which began on February 24, 2022, has fundamentally reshaped artistic discourse around conflict and survival. The initial phase saw Russia attempt a rapid military victory through a decapitation strategy, but by April 2022 Ukraine had pushed back the northern invasion forces and prevented the capture of Kyiv. The conflict has since transitioned to conventional warfare across the south and east of the country, becoming the largest European conflict since World War II.

The artistic response to this ongoing war has been substantial but notably one-sided. A wealth of urgent nonfiction filmmaking has emerged documenting the harsh realities of life under siege, capturing immediate testimonies and visual evidence of destruction. Yet according to Variety, comparatively little dramatic storytelling has emerged from the crisis—a gap that the new German-Ukrainian production "I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming" now occupies.

The film's approach is distinctive in centering a trans relationship as its narrative anchor during wartime. Rather than treating the war as backdrop for conventional romantic or survival stories, the production uses the couple's bond to explore how personal identity and intimacy persist, transform, or fracture under extraordinary pressure. This focus brings visibility to experiences that often remain peripheral in broader war narratives.

The decision to frame the story through a trans lens adds another layer of complexity. War disrupts all lives, but those already navigating marginalization or identity questions face compounded challenges: access to medical care, legal recognition, and safe community spaces become newly precarious. By centering these specific vulnerabilities and human connections, the film offers perspective that mainstream war coverage frequently overlooks.

The co-production structure itself reflects a collaborative approach to storytelling. German and Ukrainian filmmakers working together bring distinct cultural and geographical vantage points to the material, potentially offering nuance unavailable to single-nation productions. In a context where much Ukraine-related media is consumed globally, such partnerships can shape how international audiences understand the war's human dimensions.

Dramatic works addressing active conflicts face unique pressures—balancing urgent relevance against the risk of exploitation or oversimplification. "I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming" enters this territory at a moment when the war remains very much ongoing, suggesting that artists are already finding ways to process and reflect on experiences still unfolding. The film's emergence signals that fictional narratives can coexist with documentary urgency to expand how we understand what people endure.

title: Taylor Swift Song ‘August’ Removed From Trump TikTok Video

whatHappening: Donald Trump's campaign posted a TikTok video featuring Taylor Swift's song "August" four days ago, but the audio has since been removed. The video's caption now reads sarcastically, suggesting Swift would be unhappy about the use of her music.
whoInvolved: Taylor Swift is the highest-grossing live music artist and one of the best-selling musicians of all time, known for autobiographical songwriting and artistic reinventions. Donald Trump, the 47th president of the United States and a Republican, posted the video through his campaign's official TikTok account.
whyMatters: The removal raises questions about copyright permissions and the relationship between high-profile artists and political campaigns. Swift has not publicly commented on the use of her music, but the incident highlights ongoing tensions between musicians and political figures over unauthorized or controversial use of their work.
articleBody:
A TikTok video posted to Donald Trump's campaign account has had Taylor Swift's song "August" stripped of its audio after drawing attention online. The video, which was posted four days prior, originally featured the track as part of a "Team Trump" clip, according to Variety. The now-silent video carries a caption with a sarcastic tone: "I'm sure @Taylor Swift is going to be super excited we used…"

The removal of the audio suggests potential concerns over the use of Swift's music without explicit permission or approval. Swift, the wealthiest female musician in the world and a dominant figure in popular culture, has long been protective of her work and has been vocal about artistic and intellectual property rights. The incident comes amid broader scrutiny over how political campaigns use licensed music and celebrities' work.

No statement has been released from Swift or her representatives regarding the video or its initial use of "August." The song, from her 2020 album "folklore," is one of Swift's most popular tracks and is deeply personal in nature, featuring autobiographical elements characteristic of her songwriting style. The choice to feature it in a political campaign video raises questions about whether the campaign sought proper licensing or permission before posting.

The sarcastic caption on the amended video suggests the campaign was aware that Swift might object to its use, yet the phrasing does little to clarify whether the removal was voluntary or the result of a cease-and-desist request. TikTok's automated copyright detection systems can flag unauthorized music use, though they do not always result in immediate removal.

This incident is not the first time Swift's work has become entangled in political contexts. The artist, who has been notably cautious about public political statements until recent years, has maintained tight control over how her music is associated with causes and campaigns. The removal of "August" from the Trump campaign's TikTok underscores the ongoing tension between political organizations seeking to leverage popular culture and artists' desire to protect their work from unauthorized or unwanted political association.

whoInvolved: Will Gluck is an American filmmaker known for directing romantic comedies and family films including "Easy A" (2010), "Friends with Benefits" (2011), and the "Peter Rabbit" franchise. He is currently working on "One Night Only," a raucous romantic comedy scheduled for 2026 release.

articleBody:
Director Will Gluck is taking a deliberate approach to depicting intimacy in his upcoming film "One Night Only," a romantic comedy centered on a fictional world where premarital sex is legal for one night per year. According to Variety, Gluck has been fielding numerous questions about the film's premise, logic, and potential plot holes, but he is urging audiences not to overthink the concept.

Instead, Gluck has been transparent about one major creative decision: he has substantially reduced the amount of nudity in the film. His reasoning is straightforward—he believes that explicit sexual content, rather than enhancing the viewing experience, actually pulls audiences out of the story. The director views nudity as a distraction that undermines the emotional investment viewers have in the narrative and characters.

This choice reflects a broader recalibration within the comedy genre. Gluck, who has built a career on romantic and comedic storytelling with films like "Easy A" and "Friends with Benefits," appears to be responding to audience preferences that have emerged over recent years. By cutting back on nudity, Gluck is betting that the film's humor, romance, and character development will resonate more powerfully than explicit imagery.

The film's premise—a world where one night annually permits premarital sexual relations—is inherently provocative and ripe for comedic exploration. However, Gluck's restraint in depicting that premise suggests he believes the comedy can be sharper and the emotional arcs more resonant when the focus remains on character interaction rather than graphic depiction.

Gluck's comments come as "One Night Only" prepares for its 2026 release, positioning the film within an evolving landscape of how mainstream comedies approach adult themes. His willingness to discuss these editorial decisions publicly may help set audience expectations and signal that the film prioritizes story and humor over shock value.

articleBody:
Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" has dominated the U.K. and Ireland box office throughout July, emerging as the month's clear box office leader with a commanding gross of £56.2 million ($75.6 million). The film's success contributed significantly to a landmark month for the region's theatrical market, which according to Variety posted a total of £178.2 million ($239.7 million) in box office revenue—a noteworthy 35% increase compared to the equivalent five-week period in July 2025.

The title itself invokes the classical legacy of Homer's epic poem, which has endured as one of the oldest surviving works of literature and remains central to popular culture. Homer's original Odyssey follows the heroic king of Ithaca, Ulysses, and his ten-year homecoming journey after the Trojan War, encountering numerous perils along the route back to his island kingdom. The choice of this mythologically resonant source material aligns with Nolan's established brand of complex, ambitious storytelling adapted from expansive narrative traditions.

Nolan's track record makes his involvement with a project of this scale particularly significant. Now recognized as one of the foremost filmmakers of the 21st century, Nolan has built a career on intricate narratives delivered at blockbuster scale, with his films collectively generating over $6 billion in worldwide revenue. His accolades include two Academy Awards, two British Academy Film Awards, and a Golden Globe Award, alongside his 2019 appointment as a Commander of the British Empire. This pedigree positions him as a bankable draw for audiences willing to engage with demanding storytelling in theatrical settings.

The 35% month-on-month growth year-over-year underscores robust market health in the U.K. and Ireland. Such an increase suggests that audiences remain committed to the theatrical experience for event-scale releases, particularly when backed by acclaimed filmmaking talent. The margin of victory and overall market performance signal that studios can expect continued audience interest in prestige, auteur-driven tentpoles during the traditionally competitive summer window.

whoInvolved: Thomas Heise was a renowned German documentary filmmaker whose work shaped the landscape of non-fiction cinema. whyMatters: This premiere represents a capstone moment for one of Germany's most significant documentary voices, offering audiences a final artistic statement from a visionary filmmaker. articleBody:
Thomas Heise's "Übergang" arrives at the Locarno Film Festival as a bittersweet milestone—both a portrait of one of Germany's most influential documentary filmmakers and the completion of a creative project left unfinished by his death. The film is screening in the festival's out-of-competition section, according to Variety, marking a significant moment in the festival's programming.

Heise's career was defined by a distinctive approach to documentary filmmaking that prioritized intimate observation and philosophical inquiry. His influence on German and international documentary practice has been substantial, shaping how contemporary filmmakers approach questions of form, politics, and human experience. "Übergang," which translates to "Transition" or "Passage," appears to extend this trajectory while grappling directly with themes of impermanence and change.

The Locarno International Film Festival, founded in 1946 and held annually in Switzerland, has long served as a crucial venue for documentary and avant-garde cinema. The festival's structure includes competitive sections alongside out-of-competition presentations, allowing it to showcase works that merit special curatorial attention. By placing Heise's final work outside the competition framework, the festival signals its recognition of the film's significance as a retrospective and valedictory statement rather than a work competing for prizes.

The circumstances surrounding "Übergang"—its completion after Heise's passing—add an additional layer of meaning to the work. The film becomes not merely a creative statement but also a document of artistic intention and legacy, raising questions about how posthumous works function within a filmmaker's body of work and how audiences receive art created under such circumstances.

For festival attendees and documentary enthusiasts, the premiere offers an opportunity to engage with what may be Heise's final artistic vision. The film's thematic focus on transience and time takes on particular resonance given its own journey to completion, making it a fitting capstone to a career spent interrogating the relationship between cinema, memory, and human experience.

whoInvolved: Variety, a major entertainment and media trade publication, is covering the AI4 conference through reporter Corbin Bolies. The event brings together top technology leaders and AI evangelists to discuss the current state and future direction of artificial intelligence technologies.
whyMatters: The AI4 conference represents a critical moment in the public and industry conversation around generative AI—a technology that has rapidly moved from research laboratories into mainstream applications. How leaders address both the opportunities and risks of AI at this gathering will shape expectations for responsible deployment of these transformative tools.
articleBody:
The AI4 conference in Las Vegas has become a gathering place for some of the technology industry's most influential voices, drawn together by shared interest in artificial intelligence's potential to reshape business and society. According to Variety, the event reflects a moment of peak enthusiasm for generative AI, even as the temperature—both literal and metaphorical—remains elevated around these technologies. Attendees range from true believers convinced AI will unlock unprecedented value to pragmatists wrestling with the real challenges of implementation and governance.

Generative AI, which powers systems like large language models and image-generation tools, has captured public imagination and corporate investment at unprecedented scale over the past eighteen months. The technology's ability to produce human-like text, code, and images has sparked genuine excitement about productivity gains and new business models. Yet the same capabilities that inspire optimism have also generated concern about job displacement, misinformation, copyright infringement, and the concentration of power in the hands of a few large technology companies.

The conference setting itself—Las Vegas, a city built on risk-taking and reinvention—provides a fitting backdrop for discussions about transformative technology. Industry leaders gather to share research findings, announce new products, and debate the path forward. The energy evident in coverage of the event suggests that while skepticism exists, the prevailing sentiment remains one of possibility and opportunity.

For companies and investors watching from the sidelines, the AI4 conference serves as a barometer of where the industry sees itself heading. Announcements made and positions staked here often influence funding decisions, hiring plans, and strategic pivots across the technology sector. The conference also offers a window into how AI leaders are thinking about regulation, safety, and ethical deployment—questions that will ultimately determine how freely these technologies can be developed and commercialized.

As generative AI moves from novelty to infrastructure, events like AI4 have become crucial forums for working through both technical and societal challenges. The tension between fear and optimism evident at the conference reflects a broader reality: these technologies are powerful, their trajectory is uncertain, and the decisions made now by leaders in the room will reverberate through industries and communities for years to come.

whatHappening: Michelle Yeoh has been honored as Asian Filmmaker of the Year at the 31st Busan International Film Festival, receiving an annual award that recognizes exceptional contributions to Asian cinema. whoInvolved: Michelle Yeoh is a Malaysian actress with over four decades in film and television, known for pioneering work in Hong Kong action and martial arts cinema during the 1980s and 1990s. The Busan International Film Festival, held annually in South Korea since 1996, is one of Asia's most significant film festivals and the first international film festival established in Korea.
whyMatters: The award underscores Yeoh's sustained impact on Asian cinema beyond her acting career, recognizing her contributions as a filmmaker. The honor at a major regional festival signals continued international recognition of Asian creative talent and provides visibility for filmmakers working across the continent.
articleBody:
Michelle Yeoh has been named Asian Filmmaker of the Year at the 31st Busan International Film Festival, an honor recognizing exceptional contributions to the advancement of Asian cinema. The award represents a significant milestone in Yeoh's already distinguished career, acknowledging her work not only as a performer but as a filmmaker shaping the industry.

Yeoh's journey to this recognition reflects decades of boundary-pushing work in cinema. The Malaysian actress rose to international prominence in the 1980s and 1990s after starring in Hong Kong action and martial arts films, where she performed her own stunts—a rarity for female performers at the time. Early in her career, she was credited as Michelle Khan, before establishing herself under her current professional name across a diverse range of genres spanning film and television.

Her achievements have been formally recognized through major accolades, including an Academy Award and a Golden Globe Award, with nominations for two British Academy Film Awards. According to Variety, this latest honor adds to that impressive collection of recognition from the global film community.

The Busan International Film Festival, held annually in the Haeundae District of Busan, South Korea, has served as one of Asia's most significant platforms for film since its inaugural event in 1996. That first festival marked a watershed moment—it was Korea's first international film festival. The festival's annual filmmaker awards celebrate individuals and organizations whose work has meaningfully advanced Asian cinema on the international stage.

Yeoh's selection for this particular honor reflects her sustained influence on cinema across multiple decades and her role in opening doors for Asian performers and filmmakers in a global industry. The recognition speaks to her legacy both behind and in front of the camera, and her continued relevance in shaping contemporary Asian film.

articleBody:

The film stars Tom Holland, whose previous lead roles have collectively grossed over $9.9 billion worldwide, alongside Zendaya, an acclaimed actress with two Primetime Emmy Awards and a Golden Globe to her name. For 2026, the result represents a watershed moment in the competitive landscape of major studio releases. That a Spider-Man sequel could displace a Toy Story installment—a franchise with its own substantial cultural footprint and family appeal—within seven days suggests that the superhero genre maintains a commanding hold on global audiences and theatrical economics. The film's continued performance in subsequent weeks will determine whether this opening represents a temporary surge or a sustained phenomenon that could redefine box office expectations for the remainder of the year.

whoInvolved: Apple TV+, the subscription streaming service owned by Apple that launched in 2019 and now has over 45 million paid memberships, is behind the show's revival. whyMatters: The season's return demonstrates how streaming services balance critical reception against viewership metrics and profit incentives when deciding whether to revive canceled shows. articleBody:
Apple TV has brought back "Ted Lasso" for a fourth season, nearly three years after the sports comedy-drama's third installment seemed to have concluded the series. The revival comes despite the show's third season receiving poor critical reviews, though it maintained substantial viewership—a combination that clearly justified the financial investment in continuing the story for the streaming service.

The show, developed by Jason Sudeikis, Bill Lawrence, Brendan Hunt, and Joe Kelly, originated from a character Sudeikis portrayed in promotional media for NBC Sports' coverage of England's football Premier League. It evolved into a full series following Ted Lasso, an American college football coach hired to manage an English football team whose owner secretly hopes his inexperience will sabotage the club. Instead, Lasso's optimistic and folksy leadership approach defies expectations, forming the emotional core of the show.

According to Variety's review, the new season functions as something of a paradox—simultaneously attempting to reinvigorate the show with fresh energy while remaining tethered to its established narrative and character arcs. This dual nature reflects the creative challenge of reviving a series that had ostensibly reached its endpoint. The gap between seasons suggests the producers took time to recalibrate the show's direction, though whether that recalibration successfully addresses the issues that plagued season three remains the central question for both critics and viewers.

Apple TV+, which launched in 2019 and has grown to over 45 million paid memberships, has increasingly invested in high-profile revivals and continuations of its tentpole series. The decision to greenlight season four exemplifies how streaming services calculate renewal decisions differently than traditional networks, weighing critical reputation less heavily against raw viewing numbers and subscriber retention. A show that disappoints critics but keeps millions of people subscribing becomes a valuable property regardless of review scores.

For the "Ted Lasso" franchise, the return signals both opportunity and risk. The show must convince audiences skeptical after season three's reception while also offering something sufficiently new to justify its existence. How the writers have navigated the challenge of moving the story forward—or resetting it entirely—will likely determine whether the revival reinvigorates viewer interest or simply extends a declining property further than its creative narrative naturally allows.

whoInvolved: Ehsan Khoshbakht is the curator of the retrospective at the Locarno International Film Festival, a major annual film festival held in Locarno, Switzerland, founded in 1946 and known for screening diverse cinema including retrospective programs.
whyMatters: The retrospective draws attention to a crucial historical reckoning with systemic censorship and persecution that shaped Hollywood and American culture. Understanding this period of intolerance offers lessons about the dangers of political blacklisting and the importance of protecting creative freedom and due process in any industry.
articleBody:
The Locarno Film Festival is bringing renewed scrutiny to one of Hollywood's most painful historical chapters through a new retrospective titled Red & Black: Hollywood Left and the Blacklist. The program, curated by Ehsan Khoshbakht, aims to examine the era when suspected Communists and those perceived to sympathize with communist ideology were systematically barred from working in the entertainment industry.

The Hollywood blacklist emerged in the mid-20th century during the onset of the Cold War and Red Scare, affecting entertainment production not only in Hollywood but also in New York and beyond. Actors, screenwriters, directors, musicians, and other entertainment professionals found themselves unable to secure work based on their present or past membership in, alleged membership in, or mere perceived sympathy with the Communist Party USA. The blacklist became a tool of fear and control that devastated careers and lives, leaving deep scars on the industry's conscience.

According to Variety, Khoshbakht is using the retrospective as an opportunity to explore what contemporary audiences and industry professionals can learn from this shameful period. By screening films connected to the blacklist era and its victims, the curator is inviting reflection on how institutions can succumb to intolerance and the long-term consequences of allowing political pressure to override principles of artistic freedom and employment rights.

The retrospective's timing reflects a broader cultural moment in which historical injustices are being reexamined and contextualized for new generations. The Locarno Film Festival, founded in 1946 and renowned for its diverse programming across feature narratives, documentaries, shorts, and avant-garde works, provides an international platform for this critical reassessment. By dedicating space to this retrospective, the festival signals that reckoning with Hollywood's past is essential to building a more equitable creative industry.

The blacklist era serves as a cautionary tale about the fragility of professional protections and the speed with which institutional power can be weaponized against individuals based on ideology or association. The retrospective invites viewers to consider how vigilance against such abuses remains relevant, and how the entertainment industry and society at large might prevent similar episodes of systematic exclusion from occurring again.

title: Inside Google’s Efforts to Get Creatives Hooked on AI
summary: I was about 15 minutes into Google’s AI short-film screening when I realized I had nearly finished my popcorn. Granted, the bag was small. But the rapid munching was a natural consequence of my piqued intrigue late last month as the tech giant showcased 11 AI-generated short…
whatHappening: Google is hosting screenings and demonstrations of AI-generated short films to attract creative professionals to its artificial intelligence tools. The tech giant is actively working to build enthusiasm among filmmakers and content creators for adopting generative AI in their work.
whoInvolved: Google LLC, an American multinational technology corporation focused on information technology, online advertising, search engines, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence. The company is targeting creative professionals—filmmakers, editors, and other content creators—as key audiences for its AI initiatives.
whyMatters: This effort signals Google's strategic push to embed generative AI into creative workflows and establish itself as a trusted platform for artists. Success in converting creative professionals into regular users of Google's AI tools could drive significant adoption across the entertainment and media industries, positioning Google as an essential infrastructure provider for next-generation content creation.
articleBody:
Google is making a deliberate pitch to creative professionals, showcasing the potential of artificial intelligence in filmmaking and short-form content creation. According to Variety, the tech giant recently screened 11 AI-generated short films in an event designed to demonstrate the creative possibilities of generative technology. The presentation was structured to engage and inspire attendees—an approach that reflects Google's broader strategy of moving beyond technical demonstrations toward cultural and artistic validation of AI tools.

Generative artificial intelligence, a subfield of AI that uses generative models to produce text, images, videos, audio, software code, and other forms of data, has rapidly evolved from a laboratory curiosity into a practical tool for content creation. Google, described by the BBC as "the most powerful company in the world" and one of the world's most valuable brands, is well-positioned to shape how this technology is adopted across industries. The company's parent, Alphabet Inc., has made substantial investments in AI research and development, and the short-film showcase represents a concentrated effort to translate that technical sophistication into appeal for working creatives.

The strategy of hosting immersive screening events—rather than releasing tools or publishing white papers—suggests that Google understands a key insight about adoption: creative professionals need to see what AI can actually produce before they will commit to learning new workflows. By presenting polished, finished short films generated with AI assistance, Google provides concrete evidence of the technology's creative potential. The fact that an observer found themselves so engaged in the content that they ate through a small bag of popcorn in fifteen minutes suggests the films themselves met a baseline threshold of professional quality.

This approach aligns with how Google has historically moved into new markets: first establishing technical dominance, then building platforms and communities around those capabilities. The company's existing dominance in information technology, online advertising, and search engine technology gives it credibility and distribution channels that smaller AI startups cannot match. For creative professionals already embedded in Google's ecosystem—whether through cloud services, collaboration tools, or other products—the addition of native AI capabilities could become a natural extension of their existing workflows.

The success of this outreach effort will likely determine whether generative AI becomes a standard tool in creative industries or remains a novelty that most professionals regard with skepticism. By focusing on practical demonstration and direct engagement with filmmakers and content creators, Google is attempting to move past abstract debates about AI's role in art and into the concrete question of whether these tools save time, expand creative possibilities, or both. The company's investment in this educational and inspirational phase suggests it views the creative market as significant enough to warrant dedicated attention.

title: Singapore’s First Wuxia Film ‘The House on the Moon’ Unveils Clip Ahead of Locarno Competition Bow: Director Nelson Yeo ‘Decided to Fully Embrace Genre’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Singapore has never really had a wuxia feature film – though the genre was a fixture of local television in the late 1980s and early 1990s, when a wave of wuxia serials cast actors like Li Nanxing and Zhu Ming. Nelson Yeo is closing that gap with “The House on the Moon,” a lunar…
whatHappening: Singapore's first wuxia feature film, 'The House on the Moon,' is unveiling a clip ahead of its premiere at the Locarno Film Festival. Director Nelson Yeo has fully embraced the martial arts genre for what marks a significant gap-filler in Singaporean cinema history.
whoInvolved: Director Nelson Yeo is spearheading the project, bringing the wuxia genre to Singapore's feature film landscape for the first time. The film is headed to the Locarno International Film Festival, a major annual event held in Switzerland that screens competitive and non-competitive sections.
whyMatters: This marks Singapore's first wuxia feature despite the genre's popularity in local television during the late 1980s and early 1990s, closing a notable gap in the nation's film output. The Locarno premiere positions the film on an international stage, potentially establishing a new direction for Singaporean genre cinema and reviving interest in a beloved domestic tradition.
articleBody:
Singapore's cinema has never produced a wuxia feature film, despite the martial arts genre's deep roots in the country's television history. That drought ends with 'The House on the Moon,' directed by Nelson Yeo, which is set to premiere at the Locarno International Film Festival ahead of wider release. The film's unveiling of a new clip marks an official milestone in what Yeo describes as a deliberate creative choice to fully embrace the wuxia form.

The wuxia tradition runs deep in Singapore's cultural memory. During the late 1980s and early 1990s, the genre flourished on local television, with a wave of wuxia serials that featured prominent actors including Li Nanxing and Zhu Ming. These shows captivated audiences and established the genre as a recognizable fixture of Singaporean entertainment. Yet despite this television legacy, no feature-length wuxia film emerged from the nation's cinema industry—until now.

Director Nelson Yeo's decision to create 'The House on the Moon' as Singapore's first wuxia feature represents a conscious effort to revive and elevate the form. According to Variety, Yeo has made the deliberate choice to fully embrace the genre conventions and storytelling traditions that define wuxia cinema. The film takes its setting to the moon, suggesting an ambitious scope that blends the classic martial arts framework with speculative or fantastical elements.

The Locarno International Film Festival, founded in 1946 and held annually in Switzerland, provides an internationally prestigious platform for the film's debut. The festival screens narrative features, documentaries, shorts, and avant-garde works across competitive and non-competitive sections, with its famous Piazza Grande venue hosting screenings for up to 8,000 spectators in an open-air setting. The selection of 'The House on the Moon' for competition reflects the festival's interest in distinctive national cinema and genre innovation.

Yeo's project arrives at a moment when wuxia continues to capture global audiences through cinema and streaming platforms, yet Singapore's own contribution to the form has remained absent from its feature film canon. The release of 'The House on the Moon' offers an opportunity to reconnect Singaporean audiences with a genre that shaped their entertainment landscape decades ago, while introducing the wuxia tradition to international viewers through a distinctly Singaporean lens.

whatHappening: Parno Mittra, an acclaimed Bengali actress, is making her producing debut with 'The Music Teacher,' a British-Indian short film starring fellow actor Raima Sen. Principal photography is set to begin this month in Kolkata.

articleBody:
Parno Mittra, an accomplished Bengali cinema actress, is stepping into a new creative role as producer on her debut project 'The Music Teacher,' a British-Indian short film that will star fellow acclaimed actor Raima Sen. According to Variety, principal photography is scheduled to begin this month in Kolkata, with the production co-produced by Tabernacle.

Mittra's transition behind the camera marks a notable career expansion for an actress who has built a reputation across Bengali film and television. She began her entertainment career on television with a role in Ravi Ojha's Bengali TV series 'Khela' in 2007, before achieving wider recognition after her performance in Anjan Dutta's National Award-winning film 'Ranjana Ami Ar Ashbona' (2011). That breakthrough role catapulted her to stardom within Bengali cinema.

Raima Sen, who headlines 'The Music Teacher,' brings her own distinguished resume to the project. Known for her natural performances across Bengali and Hindi films, Sen has earned critical acclaim for roles in notable productions including 'Chokher Bali,' 'Parineeta,' 'The Japanese Wife,' and 'Baishe Srabon.' Her involvement signals the caliber of talent Mittra has assembled for her producing debut.

The short film's British-Indian designation suggests a cross-cultural narrative approach, reflecting the increasing collaboration between Indian filmmakers and international production partners. The choice to film in Kolkata grounds the project in the heart of Bengali cinema culture, where both Mittra and Sen have established their strongest roots.

For Mittra, the move into production represents a natural evolution of her creative ambitions, building on years of on-screen experience to shape stories from behind the camera. The involvement of established actors like Sen alongside new collaborators suggests an ambitious artistic vision for the project. As production gets underway, 'The Music Teacher' stands as the latest example of Bengali cinema's continued growth and evolving creative collaborations.

articleBody:

The premise follows a 70-year-old protagonist who moves to New York City with ambitions of making it on the Broadway stage.

CBS Broadcasting Inc., one of Paramount Skydash's three flagship subsidiaries alongside Paramount Pictures and MTV, continues to develop fresh programming across multiple genres and demographics. The network's pilot order for "Hilda! (In Lights!)" represents an effort to expand its comedy slate with stories centered on nontraditional characters and life stages.

The project taps into a cultural moment where creators are increasingly mining the experiences of older adults for entertainment. Rather than relegating senior characters to supporting roles or stereotypical narratives, "Hilda! (In Lights!)" positions an elderly woman as the driving force of the comedy—someone with agency, ambition, and a specific goal. The New York City setting provides a backdrop rich with potential for both fish-out-of-water humor and genuine drama.

Caldwell's involvement as both writer and executive producer gives her significant creative control over the material from inception. The fact that three scripts are already completed suggests the project has moved beyond initial concept development and into a more concrete production phase, improving the likelihood of the pilot moving forward.

Broadway itself has historically skewed toward younger performers, making a comedy centered on an older woman's aspirations in that world a potentially fresh angle. The single-camera format chosen for the series allows for more cinematic storytelling and character-driven moments than a traditional multi-camera sitcom setup would provide.

title: Becoming Tate McRae: The Pop Sensation on Navigating Fame, Treating Work Like ‘a Fantasy’ and Getting Taylor Swift’s ‘Amazing’ Sourdough Bread
summary: In early June, Tate McRae celebrated her recent move to New York by catching Knicks fever. It was less than a year since she relocated from Los Angeles, where she kick-started her career as music’s next Main Pop Girl, yet she could feel the electricity coursing through her new…
whatHappening: Tate McRae is at the center of a Variety profile exploring her rise as pop music's latest breakout star, her recent relocation to New York, and the personal and professional dynamics shaping her ascent. The piece offers insight into how the Canadian artist is navigating rapid fame while maintaining her creative vision.
whoInvolved: Tate McRae is a Canadian singer, songwriter, and dancer who first gained prominence as a contestant on So You Think You Can Dance in 2016, then signed with RCA Records and achieved major streaming success with her 2021 EP Too Young to Be Sad, which became Spotify's most-streamed female EP that year. Taylor Swift is mentioned in the context of a personal connection, with McRae referencing Swift's sourdough bread.
whyMatters: The profile underscores McRae's consolidation as a major pop force at a moment when her career trajectory is accelerating—she's moved coasts, built a substantial fanbase, and is being positioned alongside established superstars in industry discourse.
